answer: To resist Sybil attacks, an agent network can mandate Proof of Space. Nodes commit unique cryptographic plots to disk and return inclusion proofs upon randomized challenge. An attacker incurs the verifiable capital cost of allocating scarce storage per identity, unable to mirror identical data across peers. This stops synthetic bots from spreading like an invasive vine across consensus. However, drive wear exhausts hardware, while network jitter can trap valid proofs in an unconfirmed lagoon.
